questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I) : In the Lanthanoids, the formation of Ce+4 is favoured by its noble gas configuration.
Statement (II) : Ce+4 is a strong oxidant reverting to the common +3 state.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Statement (1) is true, Ce+4 has noble gas electronic configuration.
Statement (2) is also true. The formation of Ce4+ is favoured by its noble gas configuration, but it is a strong oxidant reverting to the common +3 state. The Eo value for Ce4+/ Ce3+ is + 1.74 Vwhich suggests that it can oxidise water. However, the reaction rate is very slow and hence Ce(IV) is a good analytical reagent.
An oxidising agent is a substance that oxidises other substances involved in the reaction by gaining or accepting electrons from them. It is also referred to as an oxidiser or oxidant.

Hence, both the statements are correct.

questions.q: The highest possible oxidation states of uranium and plutonium, respectively, are
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of Uranium is,
Rn 5f3 6d17s2

Hence, the maximum electrons it can lose is 3+1+2=6 (Inner electrons do not come out due to stability)

The electronic configuration of plutonium is, Rn 5f6 7s2

It exhibits a maximum oxidation state of +7.

questions.q: The metal ion (in gaseous state) with lowest spin-only magnetic moment value is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Ion Electronic configuration No. of unpaired electron
1 Cr2+ 3d4 4
2 V2+ 3d3 3
3 Fe2+ 3d6 4
4 Ni2+ 3d8 2

Magnetic moment(spin only) is calculated by the formula μ= n(n+2) BM.

Magnetic moment (spin only)is directly proportional to the number of unpaired electrons.

Hence, less is the number of unpaired electrons less is the magnetic moment (spin only).

As Ni2+ has the least number of unpaired electrons it has the least magnetic moment (spin only) among the given options.

questions.q: Alkaline oxidative fusion of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>MnO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> gives "<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> " which on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline solution produces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>.</mo><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> respectively are:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The alkaline oxidative fusion is a redox reaction (undergoes both oxidation and reduction simultaneously) in which a compound undergoes fusion with itself only, in the presence of a base or an alkaline solution. 

Electrolysis is a chemical process where an electric current is passed through an electrolyte, causing a non-spontaneous chemical reaction to occur, typically resulting in the decomposition of the electrolyte into its constituent elements or ions.

Alkaline oxidative fusion of MnO2 :
2MnO2+4OH-+O2→2MnO42-+2H2O

Electrolytic oxidation of MnO42- in alkaline medium.
MnO42-→MnO4-+e-

Hence, the answer is option B.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : The 4f and 5f - series of elements are placed separately in the Periodic table to preserve the principle of classification.

Statement (II) : s-block elements can be found in pure form in nature.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The Lanthanides 4f-and Actinides 5f- inner transition series of elements are placed separately at the bottom of the periodic table. Reason: (i) This prevents the undue expansion of the periodic table i.e., maintains its structure and (ii) also because their properties are different from other elements.

The main reason that s-block elements never occur in free state/nature is that these are alkali and alkali earth metals which are highly reactive. The high reactivity comes from their low ionization energy.
They have either one or two electrons in their outermost orbit so they tend to form stable products as soon as they get another element wanting electrons. Thus, s-block elements are never found in a free state in nature.
They are always found in formed compounds, such as silicates, carbonates, oxides, etc. As the elements are highly reactive, they easily accept elements or compounds.

questions.q:
The 'Spin only’ Magnetic moment for [Ni(NH3)6] 2+ is______× 10–1 BM. (given = Atomic number of Ni : 28)

Round off your answer to the nearest integer.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In the presence of ligand NH3, pairing does not occur in Ni2+ because pairing of electrons cannot create two vacant d-orbitals. Hence, nickel ion undergoes sp3d2 hybridisation and it has two unpaired electrons.

Ni2+=3d8

No. of unpaired electron =2

The spin only magnetic moment 

μ=nn+2=8=2.82 BM

=28.2×10-1 BM

x=28

questions.q: In ammonium-phosphomolybdate, the oxidation state of Mo is +_______
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Phosphomolybdate is an anion containing both phosphorus and molybdenum, with the chemical formula NH43PO4·12MoO3. 

The ammonium ion has a total charge of +3, and the phosphate ion has a total charge of -3. Therefore, the 12 MoO3 units in the compound must have a total charge of +3 - (-3) = +6.

Each MoO3 unit contains one Mo atom and three O atoms. The total oxidation state of the three O atoms is -6, since each O atom has an oxidation state of -2.

So, 

Mo + (-6) = 0 Mo = +6
